column1: # Every column here is a PRIMITIVE fact you can read off a vendor datasheet or
# a die shot. Nothing derived is stored: peak FLOP/s
# ridge point and the decode ceiling are all computed by run.py from these.
# That is the whole point - if you store the derived number you can never
# notice when it disagrees with its own inputs.
#   boost_ghz         published boost clock (blank = not published)
#   bf16_tflops_dense published 16-bit tensor peak WITHOUT sparsity
#   bf16_or_fp16      which 16-bit format that number is for
#   fp8_tflops_dense  published 8-bit tensor peak without sparsity (blank = n/a)
#   mem_gbps_per_pin  per-pin data rate (GDDR: effective; HBM: per pin)
